The operating problem

Repair shops run on conversations - but conversations get lost.

Phone calls, handwritten notes, missed follow-ups, after-hours inquiries, technician updates, and customer concerns overload shops with fragmented communication.

Missed Calls Become Lost Revenue

Busy bays, ringing phones, and after-hours questions create opportunities that disappear before anyone can act.

Front Desk Staff Juggle Too Much At Once

Calls, appointments, estimates, technician questions, and customer updates all compete for attention.

Repair Details Get Lost Between Teams

A customer concern turns into partial notes, verbal handoffs, and unclear next steps for the technician.

Customer History Lives In People's Memory

The best context often sits in a staff member's head instead of a system the whole shop can use.
